climate.overview_html: The Super El Niño is approaching its projected peak, with a Columbia Climate School analysis projecting the Niño 3.4 anomaly could reach +3.38°C between November and January — an outcome that would surpass every previous El Niño in the instrumental record. The IMO’s third extraordinary MEPC session is actively voting on the Net-Zero Framework for international shipping; UCL analysis shows a majority of member states have returned to supporting adoption after the 57–49 adjournment in October 2025 — with the outcome determining whether international shipping faces the first-ever mandatory carbon pricing regime. The EU’s Climate Resilience Strategy covering 100 vulnerable territories is expected this month alongside a Climate Insurance Alliance addressing the fact that only a quarter of climate-related economic losses in the EU are currently insured.

items.headline: El Niño 2026: Columbia Analysis Forecasts Peak Niño 3.4 of +3.38°C Nov–Jan; 75% Probability of Historic Event Exceeding All Prior Records; 2027 “Almost Certainly” the Warmest Year on Record
items.summary: A Columbia Climate School analysis published October 1 synthesizes multi-model ensemble guidance and seasonal forecast products to project the 2026 Super El Niño's likely peak. The Niño 3.4 index is projected to reach +3.38°C between November 2026 and January 2027, substantially exceeding the +2.37°C peak of the 1997–98 El Niño — the previous record in the modern observational record. The analysis assigns a 75% probability that October–December 2026 will rank as the strongest El Niño season on record. Because global mean surface temperature lags the tropical Pacific SST anomaly by approximately three to six months, 2027 is described as "almost certainly" going to be the warmest calendar year in the instrumental record, regardless of how quickly El Niño weakens. The Columbia analysis also reviews the ocean heat recharge mechanism: record upper-ocean heat content in 2024–25 loaded additional thermal energy into the Pacific, amplifying the 2026 event beyond what ENSO dynamics alone would predict.

items.headline: CAMS Atmosphere Watch 2026: 34% of Global Population Exposed to “Extremely Poor” Ozone Air Quality Jan–Sep 2026; Asia 53%; 50% of Europeans Exposed to Poor or Worse; Wildfires and Record Heat Drive Worst Year in Satellite Record
items.summary: The Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service's Atmosphere Watch 2026 report, released September 30, documents that heat waves and wildfires combined with human-caused emissions in 2026 exposed one-third of the world's population to extremely high levels of ground-level ozone. Between January 1 and September 15, 34% of the global population experienced "extremely poor" ozone air quality. Asia had the highest regional exposure at 53%; 50% of Europe's population faced poor, very poor or extremely poor ozone levels. The CAMS report emphasises the direct link between climate change and air quality: ground-level ozone forms preferentially under high temperatures, and 2026's compound hazard of record heat and record wildfire smoke has created a health emergency of global scale.

items.headline: NOAA CPC ENSO Diagnostic Discussion October 2026: Super El Niño Niño 3.4 Well Above +3°C; Peak October–November; Record SST Anomaly of 3.05°C on Sep 19; >90% Probability Very Strong Event Through NH Winter
items.summary: The October 2026 NOAA Climate Prediction Center ENSO Diagnostic Discussion confirms the Super El Niño remains at historically unprecedented levels with the Niño 3.4 SST anomaly well above +3°C. NOAA forecasters expect the event to peak during October–November 2026 before gradually weakening, remaining very strong (greater than +1.5°C) through the Northern Hemisphere winter. The advisory notes the Niño 3.4 index reached 3.05°C on September 19, a record single-day anomaly in the instrumental record extending to the 1950s. The Super El Niño is the dominant driver of current global weather anomalies: drought and fire in Southeast Asia, flooding in Southern Africa, heat stress in eastern Africa and northern South America, and severely suppressed Atlantic hurricane activity. Greater than 90% probability of a very strong El Niño persisting through NH fall-winter.

items.headline: IMO MEPC Extraordinary Session Vote Actively Under Way October 2026: Net-Zero Framework for International Shipping; UCL Analysis Shows Majority Support Has Returned; US Tariff Threats vs. First-Ever Mandatory Maritime Carbon Pricing
items.summary: The IMO's third extraordinary Marine Environment Protection Committee session is actively voting on the Net-Zero Framework for international shipping, one year after the October 2025 session adjourned 57–49 under US and Saudi pressure. University College London's Shipping and Oceans Research group analysis finds that a majority of member states have returned to supporting adoption broadly as it stood when approved in 2025. The NZF would establish a Global Fuel Standard reducing marine fuel GHG intensity and a Carbon Pricing Mechanism levying a per-tonne charge on carbon-intensive fuels, with proceeds financing clean-fuel adoption in developing nations. The Trump administration renewed its opposition, threatening tariffs, visa restrictions and port levies against supporting nations. International shipping accounts for approximately 2.89% of global GHG emissions. If adopted, the NZF would be the first-ever mandatory carbon pricing mechanism for an entire international transport sector. Status as of October 3: vote actively under way.

items.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season: Zero Hurricanes Through October 1 — Historic El Niño Wind-Shear Suppression; Eastern Pacific at 19+ Named Storms Tracking for Record Season; Stark Basin Contrast
items.summary: As of October 1, 2026, the Atlantic basin had produced zero hurricanes for the entire season — one of the most striking ENSO suppression signals in the modern record. El Niño increases vertical wind shear over the tropical Atlantic, disrupting organized convective development. In sharp contrast, the Eastern Pacific recorded 19 named storms through September 30, tracking toward the most active Eastern Pacific season on record — now at 20 storms as of October 3. The basin-to-basin contrast is one of the clearest ENSO signatures in the tropical cyclone dataset. The NHC notes the suppression mechanism is well understood; the combination with record warm SSTs could theoretically still support development if a disturbance forms before November 30.

items.headline: EU Climate Insurance Alliance Announced; Climate Resilience Strategy for 100 Vulnerable Territories Due October 2026; Only 25% of EU Climate-Related Economic Losses Currently Insured; Parametric Insurance Push to Close Protection Gap
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced in September 2026 — following the continent's worst wildfire and heatwave season — that the EU will create a Climate Insurance Alliance to increase coverage for extreme weather events. EU data shows only about a quarter of climate-related economic losses in the bloc are currently insured, with national budgets serving as the insurer of last resort. The Alliance will promote instruments including parametric insurance — where payouts trigger automatically when predefined thresholds (rainfall, temperature) are breached — and group insurance schemes. A Climate Resilience Strategy is due in October 2026, outlining risk management plans for 100 vulnerable European territories, alongside a heatwave action plan and an EU water plan targeting drought risk management. The strategy is expected imminently.

major_events.name: Typhoon Surigae (JMA No. 26) — EXTRATROPICAL TRANSITION COMPLETE OCT 3; ASIAN GAMES CLOSING CEREMONY OCT 4 AT RISK
major_events.status: EXTRATROPICAL — Surigae completed its extratropical transition on October 3 after tracking northeast along Japan’s Pacific coastline; absorbed into the mid-latitude westerly flow as a residual low; heavy rain bands continue over eastern Honshu with elevated landslide risk on rain-saturated soils following Typhoon Dujuan ($22.19 B, 162 deaths) one week prior; Asian Games closing ceremony at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium (Nagoya) on October 4 at 18:00 JST faces risk from trailing moisture plume; approximately 4,000 athletes and officials still in Nagoya under watch
major_events.impact: Heavy residual rain and landslide risk across Shizuoka, Kanagawa and Chubu Oct 3–4; outdoor Asian Games events October 4 under organizer review; approximately 1.4 million students on remote learning in Chubu region; coastal flooding risk in Tokyo Bay area; disrupted rail and road connections in eastern Honshu

major_events.name: Hurricane Rachel — EASTERN PACIFIC CATEGORY 3; 110 MPH; MOVING WESTWARD
major_events.status: ACTIVE — As of October 3, Rachel is located at approximately 19.3°N, 111.1°W — south of Baja California — with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph (Category 3) and a central pressure of 963 mb; slight weakening from a 120 mph peak due to dry mid-level air intrusion and moderate wind shear; forecast to move slowly westward then bend west-northwest as a mid-level ridge rebuilds; no land threats in current track
major_events.impact: Dangerous surf and elevated swell along Baja California Pacific coast and Socorro Island; no direct land impact forecast; shipping hazard along the Mexican Pacific coast; Rachel is the 20th named storm of the 2026 Eastern Pacific season — tracking toward a record season in stark contrast to the historic zero-hurricane Atlantic

major_events.name: Typhoon Choi-Wan (JMA No. 27 / JTWC 26W) — INTENSIFYING NEAR MARIANAS; TRACKING TOWARD OGASAWARA
major_events.status: TYPHOON — Choi-Wan intensified into a typhoon on the evening of October 2 while approximately 300 km north-northwest of Saipan; as of October 3 it is tracking northward at 15 km/h with sustained winds of 130 km/h and gusts of 205 km/h; a subtropical ridge is being eroded by a passing shortwave trough, inducing a northeastward turn toward Ogasawara Islands forecast between 36–48 hours; significant wave heights of 8.5 metres near the storm center
major_events.impact: Tropical Storm Warnings issued for Guam and Northern Marianas Oct 1–2 (now downgraded); dangerous surf across Micronesia; forecast to pass near Ogasawara Islands Oct 6–7 as a typhoon; Japan Meteorological Agency advising Ogasawara residents to prepare for typhoon conditions by mid-week

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Surigae completed its extratropical transition on October 3 after tracking northeast along Japan’s Pacific coastline, but the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games closing ceremony on October 4 at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium remains at risk from residual rain bands. A new Western Pacific system, Typhoon Choi-Wan (JTWC 26W), intensified near the Northern Mariana Islands on October 2–3, reaching 130 km/h and tracking northward toward Ogasawara. In the Eastern Pacific, Hurricane Rachel maintained Category 3 status at 110 mph while moving westward away from Baja. The new FEWS.NET October 1–7 Global Weather Hazards Summary documents Southern Africa flooding — a significant reversal from the drought forecast in last week’s edition — as El Niño’s teleconnection patterns evolve rapidly.

items.headline: Typhoon Surigae Completes Extratropical Transition October 3; Asian Games Closing Ceremony October 4 at Mizuho Park Faces Rain Risk; Landslide Alert Continues Honshu; Compound Hazard After Dujuan
items.summary: Typhoon Surigae (JMA No. 26) completed its extratropical transition on October 3, 2026, after tracking northeast along Japan's Pacific coastline and delivering heavy rainfall, gusty winds and elevated landslide risk to Honshu from Shizuoka through Kanto. Absorbed into the mid-latitude westerly flow, its trailing moisture plume continues delivering significant rainfall to eastern Honshu. Organizers of the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games are monitoring conditions closely ahead of the closing ceremony on October 4 at 18:00 JST at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium. Approximately 4,000 athletes and officials remain in Nagoya under precautionary watch. The event follows Typhoon Dujuan, which caused $22.19 billion in damage and 162 deaths one week earlier, leaving soils across mountainous Honshu at saturation and landslide risk elevated. Approximately 1.4 million students in the Chubu region remain on remote learning protocols established during the typhoon emergency.

items.headline: Hurricane Rachel October 3: Category 3 at 110 mph; Dry-Air Intrusion Causes Slight Weakening From 120 mph Peak; Moving Westward South of Baja; No Land Threat; 2026 Eastern Pacific Season at 20 Named Storms
items.summary: Hurricane Rachel (2026) maintained Category 3 status on October 3 with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph and central pressure of 963 mb, located approximately 200 miles south of Baja California Sur. The storm peaked near 120 mph before weakening as dry mid-level air entrained into the eyewall under moderate east-northeast wind shear. Rachel is moving slowly westward with a forecast bend toward the west-northwest as a mid-level ridge rebuilds. No land impacts are forecast in the current track. Rachel is the 20th named storm of the 2026 Eastern Pacific season — the most active on record — in stark contrast to the historic zero-hurricane Atlantic season, the most visible ENSO basin-to-basin wind shear contrast on record.

items.headline: Typhoon Choi-Wan (JTWC 26W) Intensifies Near Northern Mariana Islands October 2–3; 130 km/h Sustained, 205 km/h Gusts; Tracking North Toward Ogasawara; Tropical Storm Warning Previously Issued for Guam and Marianas
items.summary: Tropical Storm No. 27 (Choi-Wan) intensified into a typhoon outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility on the evening of October 2, 2026, while located approximately 306 km north-northwest of Saipan. As of October 3, Choi-Wan has maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h with gusts reaching 205 km/h and is tracking northward at approximately 15 km/h. A subtropical ridge to its northeast is being eroded by a passing shortwave trough, inducing a northeastward turn toward Ogasawara Islands forecast between 36 and 48 hours. Significant wave heights of 8.5 meters are recorded near the storm center. NWS Tiyan GU issued Tropical Storm Warnings for Guam on October 1 and 2; those warnings have since been cancelled as the system tracks away from the Marianas. Japan Meteorological Agency is advising Ogasawara Islands residents to prepare for typhoon conditions by approximately October 6–7.

items.headline: 2026 Southeast Asian Haze: Indonesia’s Worst Wildfire Season in 11 Years; ASEAN Alert Level 3 Active Since Aug 26; 12 Million People Under Thick Smog; Malaysia and Singapore Schools Closed; No Effective Legal Recourse
items.summary: Indonesia's 2026 wildfire season — its most severe in 11 years — has produced transboundary haze blanketing Sumatra, Kalimantan and much of peninsular Southeast Asia since August, exposing more than 12 million people to hazardous air quality. The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre activated Alert Level 3 on August 26, the highest tier in its three-tier haze system. Haze has forced school closures in Malaysia and Singapore, spiked emergency room visits for respiratory complaints, and disrupted aviation. Legal analysts note that ASEAN's consensus-based, sovereignty-respecting framework offers no mechanism to compel Indonesia to accelerate fire enforcement or peatland protection. The 2026 crisis has been amplified by the Super El Niño producing drought conditions across Sumatra and Kalimantan, providing optimal ignition and spreading conditions.

items.headline: FEWS.NET October 1–7 Global Weather Hazards: El Niño Strengthening; Southern Africa Flooding (Reversal From Sep 30 Drought Forecast); Abnormal Heat in Northern and Eastern Africa, Hispaniola; Central America Rain
items.summary: The FEWS.NET Global Weather Hazards Summary for October 1–7, 2026 documents a significant shift in African regional precipitation patterns driven by the Super El Niño's strengthening teleconnections. Southern Africa — including areas of South Africa, Zimbabwe and Mozambique — is now experiencing flooding in a notable reversal from the September 30 edition, which had forecast drought; this rapid evolution reflects the Indian Ocean Dipole's amplifying interaction with El Niño. Abnormal heat continues to threaten food security in northern and eastern Africa, Hispaniola and northern South America. Previously dry parts of Central America received heavy rain, alleviating short-term drought but raising flood risk in low-lying areas. The summary is issued by FEWS.NET (Famine Early Warning Systems Network) and USAID to guide food security and humanitarian response decisions.

renewables.overview_html: India’s cabinet approved a $19.3 billion Green Energy Corridor Phase-III on September 30, the largest single BESS commitment in Indian history with 50 GWh of grid-integrated storage targeting 135 GW renewable evacuation capacity by FY2033. On October 2, Enel closed its 810 MW US solar acquisition from Excelsior Energy Capital for $760 million, adding the 525 MW Faraday (Utah) and Skyhawk (Tennessee) plants to bring its North American renewables platform over 13 GW. These transactions continue the momentum documented by the IEA’s confirmation that record 800 GW of global renewable capacity was added in 2025 and its projection that renewables will overtake coal in global electricity generation in 2026.

items.headline: India Cabinet Approves $19.3 Billion Green Energy Corridor Phase-III with 50 GWh BESS; Largest Dedicated Grid Storage Commitment in Indian History; Targets 135 GW Renewable Evacuation Capacity by FY2033
items.summary: India's Union Cabinet on September 30 approved the ₹1.86 trillion ($19.3 billion) Green Energy Corridor Phase-III, including ₹500 billion for 50 GWh of battery energy storage systems across India's intra-state transmission network through FY2033. A further ₹1.37 trillion funds transmission infrastructure enabling evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable energy. The 50 GWh BESS allocation is the first dedicated storage provision under the Green Energy Corridor programme and the largest single BESS commitment in Indian history. India had commissioned just 7.5 GWh of storage capacity as of July 2026, while 140 GWh was under construction, tender or awarded. The GEC-III BESS will be deployed at generator sites or strategic grid locations to address peak-hour curtailment and meet non-solar hour demand.

items.headline: Enel Closes 810 MW US Solar Portfolio Acquisition from Excelsior Energy Capital for $760 Million; Faraday 525 MW Utah (Rocky Mountain Power PPA) + Skyhawk 285 MW Tennessee (TVA PPA); North America Portfolio Exceeds 13 GW
items.summary: Enel Green Power North America closed the acquisition of 810 MW of solar plants in the United States from Excelsior Energy Capital on September 30, 2026, for approximately $760 million in enterprise value. The portfolio comprises the Faraday Solar project (525 MW, Millard County, Utah), commercially operated under a 20-year PPA with Rocky Mountain Power (PacifiCorp), and the Skyhawk Solar development (285 MW, Tennessee) under a long-term PPA with the Tennessee Valley Authority. The acquisition — funded through Enel's operating cash flows — adds approximately $90 million annually to Enel's ordinary EBITDA. Enel's North American portfolio now exceeds 13 GW of entirely renewable assets. The closing of the remaining 205 MW wind capacity from a February 2026 portfolio agreement is expected in Q4 2026.

items.headline: ACME Solar Commissions 107 MW/437 MWh BESS Across Two Rajasthan Projects; One of India’s Largest Operational Standalone BESS Milestones; Integrates Solar Fleet’s Daytime Surplus to Evening Peak Hours
items.summary: ACME Solar Holdings commissioned 107.36 MW/437.49 MWh of battery energy storage system capacity across two projects in Rajasthan, India on October 2, 2026, one of the largest operational standalone BESS milestones in the country. The two projects will provide grid-balancing services to Rajasthan Discoms, shifting excess daytime solar generation to evening peak hours. The commissioning follows ACME's July 2026 commissioning of round-the-clock (RTC) renewable projects combining solar and storage in the same state. Maharashtra's electricity regulator has separately proposed mandatory BESS for renewable projects seeking new grid connectivity, signaling a systemic push toward integrated storage deployment across India's state utilities.

items.headline: IEA Renewables 2026: Record 800 GW Global Capacity Additions in 2025; Solar 620 GW; Renewables to Reach 50% of Global Electricity Generation by 2028; China Accounts for 65% of New Capacity
items.summary: The IEA's Renewables 2026 report confirms that global renewable energy capacity additions reached a record 800 GW in 2025, with solar photovoltaic accounting for 620 GW and wind for approximately 120 GW. China accounted for approximately 65% of all new capacity, with Europe and the United States trailing at 15% and 12% respectively. The IEA forecasts that renewables will reach 50% of global electricity generation in 2028, up from approximately 35% in 2025, driven by continued cost declines and policy support. Battery storage enabling 87 GW of combined solar-plus-storage in 2025 at an average levelized cost of $57/MWh is highlighted as the key enabling technology for this trajectory.

items.headline: IEA Electricity 2026: Renewables to Overtake Coal in Global Generation in 2026; Solar Becomes Single Largest Source in 2027; Electricity Demand Up 4.5% in 2025 Driven by Heat Pumps, EVs and AI Data Centers
items.summary: The IEA's Electricity 2026 report projects that renewable energy sources will overtake coal as the largest global electricity generation category in 2026 — the first such milestone in the history of the global power sector. Solar PV is forecast to become the single largest generation source in 2027. Global electricity demand grew 4.5% in 2025, the fastest growth rate in decades, driven by heat pump adoption, electric vehicle charging and data center expansion for AI workloads. Asia Pacific, led by China and India, now accounts for over 60% of global electricity consumption. Coal generation was approximately flat in 2025 as it displaced gas in some markets even as renewables grew.

items.headline: Alight Acquires ~2 GW Swedish Solar Development Portfolio of 40 Projects from Soltech Energy Solutions; Largest Swedish Solar M&A Transaction; Projects in Southern Sweden for Corporate PPA Offtake
items.summary: Alight, a Swedish independent power producer focused on renewable energy PPAs for corporate buyers, acquired a portfolio of 40 large-scale solar development projects with approximately 2 GW of combined pipeline from Soltech Energy Solutions. Projects are located primarily in southern Sweden at various stages from ready-to-build to late-stage permitting. The acquisition is described as the largest solar M&A transaction in Swedish history by pipeline capacity. Alight intends to develop the projects under corporate PPA structures targeting Swedish industrial and data center offtakers.

items.headline: Turkey Launches 2.4 GW Wind and Solar Auction October 2026; 1.5 GW Onshore Wind, 900 MW Solar; USD-Denominated Feed-in Tariff; Largest Turkish Renewable Tender in Three Years
items.summary: Turkey's Energy Market Regulatory Authority launched its largest renewable energy auction in three years in October 2026, tendering 1.5 GW of onshore wind and 900 MW of solar PV capacity under a USD-denominated feed-in tariff support structure. The auction is part of Turkey's 2030 target to reach 120 GW of total installed renewable capacity, up from approximately 70 GW currently. Results are expected before end-2026, with commissioning targets between 2028 and 2030. The launch follows a period of uncertainty around grid connection approvals that had constrained the pipeline.

science.overview_html: The operationalization of AI weather forecasting reached new depth with the AICON preprint documenting Deutscher Wetterdienst’s fully operational global ML forecasting system at 13 km/3-hourly resolution — the most detailed account yet of a national meteorological service running an ML model in daily operations, using DWD’s own ICON-DREAM analysis rather than ERA5. The ECMWF Anemoi framework now underpins AI operations at 17 European NMSes. Against this operational momentum, a new cluster of evaluation papers is revealing systematic weaknesses: Landsberg & Barnes (GRL) found AI weather model temperature predictions lag the current climate by 15–30 years due to training-data underrepresentation of modern extreme heat — a critical limitation for operational extreme-event guidance — while PhysMetrics.Weather provides an open framework for testing mass/energy conservation, spectral realism and dynamical balance across MLWP models.

items.headline: IMSI Workshop “Unpacking AI Weather Emulators” Concludes October 2; Three-Day Event Reviews Physical Interpretability, Extreme-Event Performance and Operational Transition Challenges for MLWP Models
items.summary: The Institute for Mathematical and Statistical Innovation (IMSI) at the University of Illinois at Chicago hosted its three-day workshop 'Unpacking AI Weather Emulators' (September 30–October 2, 2026), convening researchers from operational meteorological centers, AI laboratories and academia to examine the theoretical and practical foundations of machine-learning weather prediction. Key themes included physical interpretability of transformer-based weather emulators, representation of multi-scale atmospheric dynamics, operational transition challenges at national meteorological services, and evaluation strategies for extreme events where training data is sparse. The workshop concluded with a call for standardized physical consistency benchmarks alongside RMSE/anomaly correlation metrics, feeding into WCRP's WP-MIP evaluation standards.

items.headline: AICON (arXiv 2608.24651): DWD’s Fully Operational Global ML Weather Model Since March 2 2026; 13 km / 3-Hourly Resolution; GNN on ICON-DREAM Analysis; Outperforms ICON on Near-Surface Variables
items.summary: The AICON preprint documents Deutscher Wetterdienst's fully operational global machine learning weather forecasting model, which has been running in daily operations at DWD since March 2, 2026, following a technical operations phase beginning September 2025. Unlike most global MLWP models trained on ERA5, AICON is trained on DWD's proprietary ICON-DREAM dataset at 13 km spatial resolution and 3-hourly frequency, with 15 years of training data. The architecture uses a graph neural network with encoder-processor-decoder structure on an icosahedral multi-mesh derived from ICON's native grid, ensuring spatial consistency with training data. Routine verification demonstrates competitive skill relative to the operational ICON NWP model, with AICON particularly outperforming ICON for near-surface temperature and wind in the short-to-medium range. AICON is underpinned by the ECMWF Anemoi framework alongside MET Norway's Bris and ECMWF's AIFS.

items.headline: Temperature Bias in AI Weather and Climate Models (Landsberg & Barnes, GRL): AI Models Predict Climates 15–30 Years Out of Date; Cold Bias Strongest for Hottest Extremes; Eastern US Lags by Up to 30 Years; Training-Data Gap Identified
items.meta: Landsberg, J.B. & Barnes, E.A. · Geophysical Research Letters, 2025GL119740
items.summary: A GRL study by Jacob Landsberg and Elizabeth Barnes (Colorado State University) finds that AI weather and AI climate models produce systematic cold-biased boreal winter land temperatures resembling the climate of 15–20 years earlier than the evaluation period. In some regions — particularly the eastern United States — temperature predictions resemble climates from as much as 20–30 years in the past. The cold bias is strongest for the hottest temperature extremes, consistent with underrepresentation of modern extreme heat in training data collected predominantly before the rapid warming acceleration of the 2010s–2020s. The study examined FourCastNet V2 Small, Pangu-Weather and ACE2. A model predicting today's climate as if it were 2000–2005 will systematically underestimate extreme heat risk — the events most critical for forecasters and emergency managers. The paper calls for climate-adaptive training strategies and regular retraining as new observational data accumulates.

items.headline: ECMWF Anemoi Framework Now Underpins AI Forecasting Operations at 17 European NMSes; Shared Datasets, Infrastructure and Training Pipelines Across DWD (AICON), MET Norway (Bris), ECMWF (AIFS) and 14 Other Services
items.summary: An ECMWF Anemoi blog post documents that the collaborative European ML weather framework now supports AI forecasting operations at 17 national meteorological services, including partners as diverse as Latvia, Morocco and Slovenia. Anemoi provides three core capabilities: AI-ready datasets (a catalogue of more than 150 curated training datasets derived from ERA5, operational ECMWF data, satellite observations and Member State archives), shared ML training workflows, and operational deployment infrastructure. Three major AI forecasting systems are now underpinned by Anemoi in full operations: ECMWF's AIFS, DWD's AICON (full operations since March 2026) and MET Norway's Bris. The framework enables participating services to avoid duplicating substantial infrastructure engineering, allowing meteorological scientists to focus on model architecture and physical validation.

items.headline: PhysMetrics.Weather (arXiv 2606.10642): Open Evaluation Framework for Physical Consistency in ML Weather Models; Tests Mass/Energy Conservation, Spectral Realism and Dynamical Balance; Code Released on GitHub
items.meta: Kasteleyn, Maier, Lauer, Eyring, Gentine, Lucic · arXiv:2606.10642 [physics.ao-ph]
items.summary: PhysMetrics.Weather presents an open evaluation framework for assessing the physical realism of machine-learning weather prediction models, developed by researchers at ECMWF, DLR, Columbia University and partner institutions. The framework tests three categories of physical consistency: global conservation budgets (mass and dry-air conservation, energy balance), spectral energy distribution (whether models preserve correct spatial variance and scale-by-scale energy structure), and multi-variable dynamical balances (geostrophic balance, thermal wind, moisture conservation). Applied to several leading ML models, PhysMetrics.Weather finds widespread physical inconsistencies including energy non-conservation and spectral over-smoothing at small scales. The framework is released on GitHub as a complement to standard RMSE/ACC metrics used in MLWP benchmarking, and is feeding into WCRP WP-MIP evaluation discussions.

items.headline: WP-MIP (arXiv 2604.16643): WCRP’s Weather Prediction Model Intercomparison Project for AI, Hybrid and NWP Models; Centralized Forecast Archive; “AI-Ready” Evaluation Metrics; Open Call for Model Submissions
items.summary: The World Climate Research Programme's Weather Prediction Model Intercomparison Project (WP-MIP) is formalizing the evaluation of AI, hybrid and physical NWP models through a centralized forecast archive. The arXiv preprint (2604.16643) describes the project's objectives: identifying relative strengths and weaknesses of different modeling paradigms in operational contexts, providing guidance on fair evaluation metrics for AI weather prediction and NWP, and accelerating development across the full model spectrum. Participating verification teams are developing 'AI-ready' evaluation techniques capable of quantifying physical and dynamical consistency of AI forecast fields — including performance under all conditions, not just mean-state skill metrics. WP-MIP complements the AIMIP Phase 1 systematic evaluations and is closely tied to the IMSI Workshop themes on physical interpretability.

items.headline: Station-Based Evaluation of ML Weather Models in Northern Norway (arXiv 2609.10564): HRES Outperforms FourCastNet3 and GraphCast for Wind; All Models Substantially Underestimate Strong Winds; No Degradation Beyond Training Period
items.summary: An arXiv preprint from Norce and MET Norway evaluates FourCastNet3 (FCN3), GraphCast and ECMWF HRES for wind speed forecasting in Northern Norway — a challenging region with complex fjord topography and rapidly changing local conditions. HRES outperforms both ML models with overall RMSE of 2.89 m/s versus 2.96 m/s for FCN3 and 2.94 m/s for GraphCast. However, FCN3 performs best under high-wind conditions, operationally the most critical scenario for maritime and aviation safety. A key finding is that all three models substantially underestimate strong wind events — consistent with the spectral over-smoothing noted in PhysMetrics.Weather. Importantly, ML models show no clear degradation beyond their training periods, suggesting temporal stability even as global warming shifts baseline climate. This is one of the first systematic high-latitude MLWP evaluations and contributes to the WP-MIP evaluation corpus.

items.headline: AIMIP Phase 1 (arXiv 2605.06944): First WCRP-Endorsed Multi-Center Systematic Evaluation of AI Weather and Climate Models; Skill, Physical Consistency and Uncertainty Quantification Benchmarks Across Forecast Leads Day 1–15
items.summary: The AI Model Intercomparison Project Phase 1 (AIMIP Phase 1) documents the first WCRP-endorsed systematic multi-center evaluation of AI weather and climate models. Phase 1 coordinates evaluation across national meteorological services and research institutions, providing standardized verification protocols for skill metrics, physical consistency tests and uncertainty quantification across deterministic and probabilistic ML models, physical NWP systems and hybrid approaches at forecast leads from day 1 to day 15. Key evaluation results are expected for full publication in late 2026. The project is designed to produce publicly accessible benchmark results enabling objective comparison of model generations to support operational center decision-making on AI adoption. AIMIP Phase 1 is a companion effort to WP-MIP's operational verification archive.

items.title: TPG Raises $10 Billion for Rise Climate II; Second Private Equity Climate Fund Closes; Alterra Commits $1 Billion; NYC Employees’ Retirement and Michigan Retirement Systems Among LPs
items.body_html: TPG has closed TPG Rise Climate II at $10 billion in committed capital, making it one of the largest dedicated climate private equity funds ever raised. The fund targets clean energy, electric transportation, sustainable materials and industrial decarbonization. Rise Climate II is led by former US Treasury Secretary Hank Paulson as executive chairman. Notable LPs include Alterra (the UAE-backed climate investment vehicle) committing approximately $1 billion, alongside the New York City Employees’ Retirement System and the State of Michigan Retirement System. The raise builds on the Rise Climate I platform (launched 2021) and brings TPG’s total climate investment AUM to among the largest in private markets globally.

items.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B for Drone-Based Cloud Seeding; First Private Company to Physically Validate Cloud-Seeding Results; 82 Seeding Signatures, 145 Million Verified Gallons
items.body_html: Rainmaker raised $100 million in Series B funding from NOA VC, Upfront Ventures, DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital and Dream Ventures to scale its drone-based cloud seeding platform. Founded in 2023 by Thiel Fellow Augustus Doricko, Rainmaker deploys weather-resistant UAVs to release silver iodide into supercooled liquid water clouds, triggering glaciogenic ice crystal formation. The company became the first private entity to physically validate cloud-seeding results, recording 82 unambiguous seeding signatures producing more than 145 million verified gallons of freshwater over four months. Total funding is now $131.3 million across three rounds. With water scarcity intensifying under the Super El Niño, the round highlights a broader investor shift toward climate adaptation and weather modification infrastructure.

items.title: Plenitude Completes €1.56 Billion Capital Hike from Eni and Ares Management; Joint Control Structure; Eni’s Renewables Arm Deconsolidated at €13.1 Billion Enterprise Value
items.body_html: Eni’s renewables arm Plenitude completed a €1.56 billion non-proportional capital increase on October 1, with Ares Management subscribing €1.08 billion and Eni subscribing €0.48 billion. The transaction implies a pre-money equity value of €10.75 billion (€13.1 billion enterprise value). Post-transaction shareholding: Eni 65.03%, Ares 26.24%, EIP 8.73%. The new governance structure grants Eni and Ares joint control over Plenitude, triggering deconsolidation from Eni’s balance sheet — structurally separating Eni’s renewables ambitions from its oil-major financials. Ares previously acquired a 20% interest in Plenitude in 2025 for approximately €2 billion.

items.title: NextEra’s $67 Billion Dominion Energy Acquisition: Shareholders Approve; Virginia Governor Spanberger “Deeply Skeptical”; FERC, NRC and Five State Commissions Reviewing; Close Expected H2 2027
items.body_html: Shareholders of both Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy approved the proposed $67 billion combination in September 2026, a critical milestone for a deal that would create the largest utility in US history with approximately 110 GW of generating capacity. The transaction requires regulatory approvals from FERC, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and public utility commissions in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina. Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger has intervened directly in the SCC review, calling herself “deeply skeptical” of consumer benefit; the companies responded by doubling bill relief commitments to four years and pledging 1,000 new Virginia jobs. The merger close is expected in H2 2027. The deal would give NextEra — the world’s largest wind and solar operator — access to Dominion’s regulated Virginia utility serving a fast-growing AI data center corridor.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance Announced; Climate Resilience Strategy for 100 Territories Due This Month; Only 25% of EU Climate Losses Insured; Parametric and Group Insurance Products to Close Protection Gap
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the EU will form a Climate Insurance Alliance to increase coverage for extreme weather following the continent’s worst wildfire and heatwave season. EU data shows only a quarter of climate-related economic losses are currently insured, with national budgets as the insurer of last resort. The Alliance will promote parametric insurance (payouts triggered automatically when temperature or rainfall thresholds are breached) and group insurance schemes. The EU Climate Resilience Strategy covering 100 vulnerable European territories is expected in October 2026 — opening commercial opportunities for climate-native risk modellers such as Reask, Jupiter Intelligence and Cape Analytics alongside established cat model vendors.
